rationale: The provided literature does not support the hypothesis. While YWHAZ is linked to neurodevelopmental delay, intellectual disability, and behavioral abnormalities (Popov-Chang syndrome; OMIM #618428), the retrieved sources provide no cohort comparisons, phenotypic frequency breakdowns, or systematic assessments demonstrating that differentiation from Miller-Dieker syndrome or YWHAE-related microdeletion syndromes specifically relies on the absence of classic lissencephaly/pachygyria and severe congenital heart defects.

evidence.text: YWHAZ variants are linked to intellectual disability and global developmental delay, with functional modeling showing cognitive and morphological abnormalities in knockin models, but without cohort comparison to Miller-Dieker syndrome or YWHAE microdeletions.

evidence.text: OMIM cataloging establishes Popov-Chang syndrome (OMIM #618428) as an autosomal dominant disorder caused by YWHAZ variants, but lacks phenotype frequency tables or diagnostic algorithms comparing it to 17p13.3 microdeletion syndromes.

conflicts: The hypothesis assumes a clinically tested differential framework based on the absence of lissencephaly and congenital heart defects, but the available literature lacks systematic clinical cohort studies comparing YWHAZ patients to Miller-Dieker or YWHAE microdeletion cohorts.

new_directions.question_text: What is the systematic neuroimaging and echocardiographic spectrum across all molecularly confirmed Popov-Chang syndrome patients in published cohorts?
new_directions.rationale: Evaluating brain MRI findings (e.g., gyration, myelination, corpus callosum) and cardiac evaluations in all known YWHAZ cases will define whether lissencephaly and congenital heart defects are genuinely absent.

new_directions.question_text: How do clinical features of isolated point mutations in 14-3-3 protein genes (YWHAZ, YWHAE) contrast with contiguous gene deletions on 17p13.3?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying the specific phenotypic contribution of 14-3-3 isoform dysfunction versus PAFAH1B1 deletion will resolve whether structural brain malformations uniquely distinguish these entities.
